title: Theatre — Minimum Requirements
notes: Section opens with a cross-reference (page 53): 'Other requirements are as stated under "Minimum requirements for all types of Health Institutions"' — the common all-institutions module applies in addition to these items. The section includes a 'POLICY ON RECOVERY ROOM STAFF' passage (pages 57-59); its concrete staffing/process obligations are captured as items, while the following policy narration is context only: staff qualifications, staffing levels, standardised minimum equipment, clinical techniques and clinical competence to decide next therapeutic manoeuvres are 'critically important for successful outcomes' (page 57); 'There is no absolute numbers of staffing levels, but state of occupancy and condition of patients dictate how best to deal with staffing levels. This should be determined at the point of providing anaesthetic service' (page 57); as a patient emerges from unconsciousness and begins to cooperate, 'one nurse could look after two patients on adjacent stations' (page 57); a patient arriving in the recovery room has a variable level of consciousness, from fully conscious (local or regional anaesthesia) to comatose (page 58); some patients may be restless or agitated post-operatively (pain, fear, full bladder, child) and may require more than one staff member until settled — self-injury is a risk (page 58); 'It is difficult to give guidance on the exact numbers of staff required' — staffing levels depend on case mix, numbers of patients and number of operating lists per session (page 59); staffing the recovery room is described as 'an ongoing intractable problem' — all staffing statements are minimal staff-to-patient ratios dependent on the clinical status of the patient, it 'remains doubtful that a magic formula can be developed', and safe staffing 'is still dependent on the expertise of the Charge Nurse who can adjust staffing if necessary on a day to day basis' (page 59).

Anaesthetic and post anaesthetic care is administered in specifically designated, equipped, and staffed registered hospitals/institutions by appropriately qualified and registered personnel or trainees under supervision of registered clinicians

The Anaesthetist leads a team of medical and nursing practitioners charged with the responsibility of ensuring complete recovery from the now undesired effects of anaesthetic drugs; pain control and stabilisation of vital functions is also an important consideration for this team especially in the first 24 hours
The recovery room charge Nurse should be able to vary staff levels very quickly and almost instantly, and call out for help if needed in a matter of an instant

Should patient condition deteriorate suddenly and unexpectedly, the Nurse immediately calls the Doctor and resuscitation team for help, which should be accorded in a matter of seconds; one patient may be attended to by a team of medical professionals as assessed appropriate in a rapidly changing situation (e.g. cardio pulmonary resuscitation)
items.conditional: applies when patient condition deteriorates suddenly and unexpectedly

items.requirement: In transporting a postoperative patient to the recovery room, the anaesthetist, the scrub nurse and a porter shall transport a stable patient lying in a hospital bed, appropriately monitored
The recovery room should receive the patient with a natural airway

Upon arrival, the anaesthetist attaches minimum monitors and fully evaluates the patient: pulse oximetry, electrocardiograph, pulse, automated interval blood pressure monitor and temperature, amongst others
items.reviewReason: Manual wording is garbled: 'These are pulse oximetry, conscious electrocardiograph pulse, automated interval blood pressure monitor and temperature, amongst others' (page 58) — the exact intended monitor list ('conscious electrocardiograph pulse') is unclear.

items.requirement: The anaesthetist physically hands over explained, written-down post-operative instructions for the care of the patient to the Nurse taking care of the patient in the recovery room, and ensures that there is complete understanding of the instructions; the Nurse examines the patient
Upon the Nurse accepting responsibility for the patient, the vital functions observations are documented
An accurate timed observation of respirations, pulse, blood pressure, pulse oximetry, amongst others, is documented

Reception of patient (patient may be unconscious or emergent from that state): staff ratio 1:2 (one patient / two nurses) to undertake handover, prioritise immediate care and set up monitoring; the skills of the first nurse must be appropriate for the acuity of the case; the helper may be a novice nurse or member of the perioperative team

Stabilisation period (self ventilating with no airway adjuncts or needing respiratory assistance): staff ratio 2:1 (two patients / one nurse); skills of nurse must be appropriate to acuity of cases; if the patient's condition deteriorates staff must be reallocated promptly

Fit for discharge (has met all local discharge criteria — is stable and comfortable): staff ratio 3:1 (three patients / one nurse); the nurse looking after three patients must be experienced and may be assisted by a novice or member of the perioperative team

No fewer than two staff (of whom at least one must be a registered practitioner) should be present when there is a patient in the recovery room who does not fulfil the criteria for discharge to the ward
items.quantity: no fewer than two staff, of whom at least one must be a registered practitioner

items.requirement: Until patients can maintain their airway, breathing and circulation they must be cared for on a one-to-one basis
At least two appropriately trained staff should be present in the recovery room while there is a patient who does not fulfil the criteria for discharge to the ward
items.quantity: at least two appropriately trained staff
items.reviewReason: Near-duplicate of the earlier bullet on the same page: 'No fewer than two staff (of whom at least one must be a registered practitioner) should be present...' vs 'At least two appropriately trained staff should be present...' — the two statements differ on the required qualification (registered practitioner vs appropriately trained) and the manual does not reconcile them.

items.requirement: Auditing variables that affect staff-patient ratios is recommended (delayed discharge being one important factor)

The anaesthetist is responsible for the discharge of the patient to a suitable ward from the recovery room; in the alternative, the nurse attending the patient shall use agreed-on, preferably written-down, discharge criteria to send the patient to a prescribed place of further care
items.alternatives: the attending nurse may discharge using agreed-on, preferably written-down, discharge criteria

items.requirement: The Nurse will read out instructions of care to the ward nurse upon handover, verify that the patient is stable and in satisfactory condition, and may point out any areas of care requiring closer attention

Fully recovered patients not yet collected by ward staff remain the responsibility of recovery room nursing staff; one nurse can look after 4 such coherently communicating, comfortable patients, provided patients are in adjacent care stations and help from a nurse aid is afforded
items.quantity: one nurse per 4 coherently communicating, comfortable patients
items.conditional: patients must be in adjacent care stations, with help from a nurse aid afforded

items.requirement: The general supervision of the patient condition is the responsibility of the anaesthetist, who shall be easily accessible to the patient in an appropriate time to deal with complications as requested by the nursing staff
